headline: RBI consolidates Domestic Money Transfer rules into DMT Directions, 2026
summary_points: RBI has issued the Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026 under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The Directions consolidate existing DMT instructions and repeal the circulars of October 5, 2011 and July 24, 2024.
They are effective immediately and apply to banks and authorised payment system operators and participants; card-to-card transfers are excluded.

rows: Remitting bank records beneficiary name and address
Cash Pay-in: walk-in at branch via NEFT
Remitter registered with verified mobile number and self-certified OVD
Cash Pay-in: via BCs, ATMs etc.
Every transaction validated by Additional Factor of Authentication
Velocity checks, customer alerts, investigation of unusual credit spurts, reporting of suspicious transactions
Only RBI-approved payment systems; reasonable charges permitted
Covered by the RB-Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026

who_is_affected: Scheduled commercial banks (including RRBs and co-operative banks), authorised payment system operators and participants, and Business Correspondents offering domestic money transfer services.
action_required: Review DMT processes, limits, KYC and AFA checks, transaction message identifiers and monitoring systems against the new Directions, and note that earlier circulars stand repealed.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026 on November 11, 2026, consolidating existing instructions on small-value cash-based remittances.

Key points:
- Effective immediately; issued under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
- Cash Pay-out: ₹10,000 per transaction, ₹25,000 monthly ceiling per beneficiary.
- Cash Pay-in: up to ₹50,000 via NEFT for walk-in customers at branches; ₹5,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 monthly per remitter through BCs/ATMs.
- Remitters registered with verified mobile number and self-certified OVD; AFA required for each transaction.
- Velocity checks, alerts and reporting of suspicious transactions are mandated.
- Circulars of October 2011 and July 2024 on DMT are repealed.

Banks, payment system operators and BCs should map their DMT processes to the new Directions.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
